content: The progression of β-cell destruction in immune-mediated diabetes varies significantly among individuals. In certain cases, particularly in children, the destruction of β-cells occurs rapidly. This rapid destruction often results in the early onset of severe hyperglycemia and diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). In contrast, adults frequently retain partial β-cell function for a longer duration. This residual function allows them to initially avoid DKA. However, as β-cell function progressively declines, these individuals eventually become insulin-dependent and are at increased risk of developing DKA. Low or undetectable levels of plasma C-peptide serve as an indicator of minimal or absent endogenous insulin production. This is a characteristic feature observed in the later stages of type 1 diabetes.
